title: Ordinary etale derived direct-image composition and its coherence
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z\xrightarrow{h}W$ be arbitrary morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Work in $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with constant-ring module direct images and their right-derived functors [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Write $Q_T$ for localization of bounded-below complexes of module sheaves at quasi-isomorphisms. For every composable pair there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$d_{g,f}:R(gf)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rf_*.$$
Its normalization is the following: if $I$ is a bounded-below complex of injective $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $X$, then, under the canonical computation of all three derived direct images on $I$ and $f_*I$, the component $d_{g,f,Q_XI}$ is the class of the degreewise sheaf comparison $(gf)_*I\cong g_*f_*I$ induced by the canonical fibre-product associativity isomorphisms. These normalizations determine the comparison uniquely. There are canonical identity comparisons $d_T:R(\mathrm{id}_T)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$, normalized on such complexes by the identity direct-image comparison. They satisfy
$$(Rh_*d_{g,f})\circ d_{h,gf}=(d_{h,g}Rf_*)\circ d_{hg,f}:R(hgf)_*\longrightarrow Rh_*Rg_*Rf_*,$$
and
$$(d_YRf_*)\circ d_{\mathrm{id}_Y,f}=\mathrm{id}_{Rf_*},\qquad(Rf_*d_X)\circ d_{f,\mathrm{id}_X}=\mathrm{id}_{Rf_*}.$$
No finiteness, properness, residue-characteristic or coefficient-invertibility hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Write $c_{g,f}:(gf)_*\to g_*f_*$ and $u_T:(\mathrm{id}_T)_*\to\mathrm{id}$. Construct these first on module sheaves using [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For $V\to Z$ etale, the map $a:(V\times_ZY)\times_YX\to V\times_ZX$ preserving the projections to $V,X$ is an isomorphism: its inverse has projections $(v,f(x)),x$. The universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] verifies both inverse identities. Put $(c_{g,f,F})_V=F(a)$, so it has exactly the required direction $F(V\times_ZX)\to F((V\times_ZY)\times_YX)$. Put $(u_{T,F})_V=F(b)$, where $b:V\to V\times_TT$ has projections $\mathrm{id}_V,V\to T$. Naturality in $V$ follows because the two scheme maps have the same projections; naturality in $F$ is the naturality of a sheaf morphism at $a,b$. These maps are $\Lambda$-linear: restriction respects the module action, and pullback of each constant scalar along $a,b$ is that same scalar. Inverses come from $a^{-1},b^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, underived comparison made explicit from the direct-image formula; fibre-product universal property

proof.text: The comparisons just constructed obey the underived associativity and unit equations. At $V\to W$, both associativity composites are obtained by applying $F$ to the map from $((V\times_WZ)\times_ZY)\times_YX$ to $V\times_WX$ that preserves the projections to $V$ and $X$. The two maps are equal by [def-pc-fibre-product]; contravariance gives $(h_*c_{g,f})c_{h,gf}=(c_{h,g}f_*)c_{hg,f}$. For either unit composite the resulting map from $V\times_YX$ to itself preserves both projections, hence is the identity. Thus $(u_Yf_*)c_{\mathrm{id}_Y,f}=\mathrm{id}$ and $(f_*u_X)c_{f,\mathrm{id}_X}=\mathrm{id}$. These are equalities of natural transformations of module sheaves, and therefore hold degree by degree for complexes too.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, underived associativity and unit comparisons underlying the composition formula; explicit universal-property verification

proof.text: For every scheme map $v$, constant-coefficient module inverse image $v^{-1}$ is exact and left adjoint to $v_*$ by clause (3) of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. It therefore preserves monomorphisms, and [lem-exc-rg-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] applies to this adjunction: $v_*$ sends injective module sheaves to injective module sheaves. It is additive by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Hence it acts on complexes and homotopies; a zero term stays zero. In particular $f_*I$, $g_*f_*I$ and all composite direct images of a bounded-below injective complex $I$ are again bounded-below complexes of injectives. This uses the constant ring identification in the cited exactness proposition, not flatness of a scheme morphism.

proof.text:
The module categories have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. For every edge $v$ denote the natural derived-functor map by $\alpha^v_L:Q(v_*L)\to Rv_*(QL)$. [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] gives this map and says it is invertible whenever $L$ is a bounded-below injective complex. For such $I$ put
$$t_{g,f,I}=Rg_*(\alpha^f_I)\circ\alpha^g_{f_*I},\qquad D_{g,f,I}=t_{g,f,I}\circ Q(c_{g,f,I})\circ(\alpha^{gf}_I)^{-1}.$$
Step 3 ensures that $\alpha^g_{f_*I}$ is invertible, so $D_{g,f,I}:R(gf)_*(QI)\to Rg_*Rf_*(QI)$ is an isomorphism. Naturality of $\alpha$ and $c$ shows that $D_{g,f,I}$ commutes with every $Q(k)$ for a chain map $k:I\to J$. Additive functors preserve the chain-homotopy equation, so the same assertion holds for homotopy classes. This formula is precisely the stipulated normalization, with all three computation isomorphisms displayed.

proof.text:
For $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ choose $e:QI\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ with $I$ bounded below and injective, using [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Write $A=R(gf)_*$, $B=Rg_*Rf_*$, and define
$$d_{g,f,K}=B(e)\circ D_{g,f,I}\circ A(e)^{-1}.$$
For another choice $e':QJ\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents $(e')^{-1}e$ by a homotopy class $k:I\to J$. The equation $B(Qk)D_{g,f,I}=D_{g,f,J}A(Qk)$ from step 4 proves equality of the two displayed formulas after substituting $e=e'Qk$. For a map $r:K\to K'$, represent $(e')^{-1}re$ by a homotopy class in the same way; that equation gives $B(r)d_K=d_{K'}A(r)$. Thus these components form a natural isomorphism. Any natural transformation with the prescribed components on $QI$ must satisfy the displayed conjugation formula by naturality at $e$; hence it equals $d_{g,f}$.

source.place: Tags 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist; 070J, lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective; 070I, lemma-K-injective, (3); explicit conjugation argument

proof.text: For the identity map on $T$ set $D_{T,I}=Q(u_{T,I})\circ(\alpha^{\mathrm{id}_T}_I)^{-1}:R(\mathrm{id}_T)_*(QI)\to QI$. The map $\alpha^{\mathrm{id}_T}_I$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Naturality of $u_T$ and $\alpha$ makes $D_{T,I}$ natural on chain maps and on homotopy classes. Apply exactly the conjugation formula of step 5, now with $A=R(\mathrm{id}_T)_*$ and $B=\mathrm{id}$, to obtain $d_T$. The representative existence and the Hom bijection used there are [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. This gives the required identity normalization and its uniqueness.

proof.text:
Evaluate the associativity equation at $QI$. Step 3 permits computing with $I,f_*I,g_*f_*I$. Put
$$t=Rh_*Rg_*(\alpha^f_I)\circ Rh_*(\alpha^g_{f_*I})\circ\alpha^h_{g_*f_*I}.$$
Expanding the left side with step 4 gives
$$t\circ Q((h_*c_{g,f,I})\circ c_{h,gf,I})\circ(\alpha^{hgf}_I)^{-1}.$$
Indeed the two occurrences of $Rh_*(\alpha^{gf}_I)$ cancel, and naturality gives
$$Rh_*Q(c_{g,f,I})\circ\alpha^h_{(gf)_*I}=\alpha^h_{g_*f_*I}\circ Q(h_*c_{g,f,I}).$$
For the right side first use naturality of $d_{h,g}$ at $\alpha^f_I:Q(f_*I)\to Rf_*(QI)$, then apply its normalized formula at $Q(f_*I)$. Cancellation of $\alpha^{hg}_{f_*I}$ leaves
$$t\circ Q(c_{h,g,f_*I}\circ c_{hg,f,I})\circ(\alpha^{hgf}_I)^{-1}.$$
Step 2 identifies the middle factors, proving equality at $QI$. Every object is isomorphic to such a $QI$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], so naturality at that isomorphism proves equality everywhere. The natural maps $\alpha$ and their injective computation are those of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective].

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; derived.tex Tags 05TH and 013K; associativity checked by expanding the normalized comparisons

proof.text:
For the left unit, naturality of $d_Y$ at $\alpha^f_I:Q(f_*I)\to Rf_*(QI)$ and its formula in step 6 give, after inserting step 4,
$$(d_YRf_*)_{QI}\circ d_{\mathrm{id}_Y,f,QI}=\alpha^f_I\circ Q(u_{Y,f_*I}\circ c_{\mathrm{id}_Y,f,I})\circ(\alpha^f_I)^{-1}=\mathrm{id}.$$
For the right unit use naturality of $\alpha^f$ at $u_{X,I}:(\mathrm{id}_X)_*I\to I$; the expansion is
$$(Rf_*d_X)_{QI}\circ d_{f,\mathrm{id}_X,QI}=\alpha^f_I\circ Q(f_*u_{X,I}\circ c_{f,\mathrm{id}_X,I})\circ(\alpha^f_I)^{-1}=\mathrm{id}.$$
In both cases the last equality is the underived unit equality in step 2. The $\alpha^f_I$ and other cancelled computation maps are invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] and step 3. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] and naturality extend the equations from $QI$ to every $K$. None of these constructions used finiteness, properness, torsion, or invertibility of a coefficient.
